conceptTag: Choose where to play on a small budget
readerTitle: Twenty thousand dollars, one kitchen: where would you play?
caseNote: 가상 시뮬레이션 (야간 근무자 대상 식사 사업) · 소프트웨어 적용은 softwareNote · 모든 인물과 상황은 설명용
insight: 예산이 작을수록 모두를 상대할 수 없으므로, 이길 수 있는 좁은 자리를 고르고 그 자리를 지키는 선택을 이어 가는 것이 전략이다.
misconception: 예산이 적으면 시장을 넓게 잡고 들어오는 주문을 다 받아야 살아남는다.

sources.text: Lafley, A.G. & Martin, R. (2013). Playing to Win: How Strategy Really Works. Harvard Business Review Press. (where to play, how to win)
Porter, M. (1996). What Is Strategy? Harvard Business Review. (trade-offs, fit, strategy vs operational effectiveness)
모든 인물, 금액, 상황은 설명용 가상 시뮬레이션

factChecks.note: 전체가 가상 시뮬레이션입니다. 실제 수치나 기업 사실은 쓰지 않았습니다. $20,000 예산과 카페 20곳은 설명용 가정입니다.
배달 앱 수수료는 구체적 비율 없이 '수익을 깎는다'로만 표현했습니다. 국가·플랫폼마다 다르므로 수치를 추가하지 마세요.
takeaway의 개념 매핑(STR-01-04, 01-02, 01-06, 01-01)이 유닛 내 레슨 제목과 일치하는지 게시 전 확인하세요.

cards.title: $20,000 and a kitchen rented by the hour.
body: Mina has $20,000 in savings and a shared kitchen she can rent by the hour. She wants to start a meal business.
She can't afford to serve everyone. Every dollar spent in one place is a dollar she can't spend in another.
You'll make four calls for her, one after another. Each one builds on the last.

image.label: A cook in a small shared kitchen with a jar of savings
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 작은 공유 주방에 선 요리사 한 명, 조리대 위에 '$20,000'이라고 적힌 저금통. 창밖은 밤의 도시. 실제 브랜드나 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Who should Mina feed?
body: Near her kitchen, Mina sees three options. Downtown offices, with about 20 cafés within a few blocks. A big hospital and two warehouses with night shifts, where only vending machines and a gas station are open after 10 p.m. Or delivery apps across the whole city.

options.feedback: Huge demand, but she'd fight 20 established cafés on price and speed. Much of her budget would go just to getting noticed.

options.text: Night-shift workers at the hospital and warehouses
options.feedback: A smaller market, but a clear need (a hot meal at 2 a.m.) and almost no rivals. Her small budget is enough to win here.

options.text: Everyone in the city, through delivery apps
options.feedback: She reaches many customers fast. But app fees cut into every order, and she becomes one listing among hundreds with nothing that sets her apart.

cards.softwareNote: A software founder faces the same call. "Scheduling for all small businesses" means fighting big, well-funded tools. "Scheduling for dental clinics" is a market a small team can actually win.

cards.eyebrow: Call 2 · What to say no to
cards.title: Say you chose the night shift. Now requests pour in.
body: Two months in, nurses are ordering again and again. Three requests arrive: a nurse wants Mina to cater her sister's wedding for 150 guests. Office workers ask for a lunch menu. A warehouse manager wants a standing order for his night crew.
Mina can't do all three well. What does she do?

options.text: Take the wedding. One big payday helps the budget
options.feedback: Good money once, but it costs a weekend of daytime cooking, rented equipment and a tired team on Monday night. Her real customers get a worse meal.
A small test limits the risk. But it splits her attention and pulls her back into the crowded fight she chose to avoid.

options.text: Take the warehouse order and politely decline the rest
options.feedback: She gains steady, predictable volume from exactly the customers she chose. Saying no keeps her focused where she can win.

cards.title: Say you said yes only to the warehouse. Now build the system.
body: Night workers can't leave their posts, and their breaks are short. Which set of choices fits together best?

image.label: Meals delivered to a night-shift break room
image.brief: 밤 2시 병원 휴게실. 간호사와 창고 직원들이 이름표 붙은 따뜻한 도시락을 받는 장면. 벽시계가 2:00을 가리킴. 실제 병원·기업 로고 없음.

options.text: Text pre-orders until 9 p.m., one batch cook, delivery to break rooms at fixed times, hearty meals that reheat well
options.feedback: Each choice supports the others. Pre-orders make batch cooking possible, batches cut waste, and fixed delivery times match fixed breaks.

options.text: Open a small shop near the hospital until 3 a.m. and cook to order
options.feedback: Rent and staff for quiet hours drain the budget fast. And her customers often can't leave their posts to walk over.

options.text: Option A's system, but with a rotating menu of 15 dishes
options.feedback: Variety pleases people. But 15 dishes break the single batch, so waste and cooking time climb.

cards.title: Say you built the pre-order system. A year later, a chain moves in.
body: A 24-hour convenience chain opens next to the hospital. It sells hot food for less than Mina charges. Some nurses start trying it.

options.text: Cut prices to match the chain
options.feedback: She can't outlast a chain on price. Each meal leaves her less money, and customers learn to judge her only on price.

options.text: Cut costs: cheaper ingredients, faster cooking
options.feedback: Running leaner always helps, but the chain can do the same. Doing things more efficiently is not the same as doing something different.

options.text: Lean into what the chain can't do: delivery to the ward at break time, dishes the staff ask for
options.feedback: The chain sells food at a counter. Mina brings dinner to people who can't leave their posts. That difference is hard for the chain to copy.

cards.title: Narrow is a bet, not a guarantee.
body: A small market can turn out to be *too* small. Mina should watch for early signs: repeat orders, customers telling coworkers, and waste going down.
If the night shift alone can't support her, she can widen to nearby groups with the **same need**, such as airport crews or security teams. She keeps her system instead of starting over.
Choices made on a tight budget also need a fresh look as the business grows.

cards.title: A small budget forces strategy. Use it.
body: Each of your four calls used one idea from this unit:
list: **Call 1, Where to play:** pick customers you can win, not the biggest crowd
**Call 2, What not to do:** saying no protects your focus
**Call 3, Fit:** choices that support each other beat good choices on their own
**Call 4, Strategy vs efficiency:** running leaner can be copied, being different is harder to copy
cards.callout: **Try it today:** write down the one customer group you could serve better than anyone nearby, and one request you'll turn down this month to keep serving them.
